info.title: mcpd
info.description: The canonical description of mcpd's data model and HTTP surface. Every SDK type, every generated docs page and the OpenAPI document are produced from this file. Nothing downstream is hand-written.

SpanKind.description: What an operation *is*. The kind drives how a span is rendered in the waterfall, which attributes are meaningful, and which metrics are auto-extracted from it.

x-enumDescriptions.agent_run: One agent invocation. Usually the root of a trace.
x-enumDescriptions.model_generation: One logical generation: everything from the first request to the final answer, including every intermediate step.
x-enumDescriptions.model_step: One step inside a generation. A generation that calls tools twice has three steps.
x-enumDescriptions.model_inference: The provider round-trip alone, excluding processors and tool execution. Measure pure model latency here.
x-enumDescriptions.model_chunk: A single streamed chunk. Recorded as an event, not a duration.
x-enumDescriptions.client_tool_call: A tool the calling client executes. The server records the marker; the client returns the detail.
x-enumDescriptions.provider_tool_call: A tool the model provider executes server-side, such as hosted web search or code execution.
x-enumDescriptions.mcp_tool_call: A tool reached over the Model Context Protocol.
x-enumDescriptions.workflow_run: One workflow execution. Usually the root of a trace.
x-enumDescriptions.workflow_conditional: A branch point, with the conditions it evaluated.
x-enumDescriptions.workflow_conditional_eval: One condition evaluated inside a branch point.
x-enumDescriptions.workflow_loop: A loop construct: foreach, do-while or do-until.
x-enumDescriptions.workflow_wait_event: A wait for an external event, with its timeout.
x-enumDescriptions.memory_operation: A read from or write to agent memory.
x-enumDescriptions.rag_ingestion: One ingestion pipeline run: load, chunk, extract, embed, upsert.
x-enumDescriptions.rag_vector_operation: Vector store I/O: query, upsert, delete or fetch.
x-enumDescriptions.rag_action: A RAG-specific transform: chunk, extract metadata or rerank.
x-enumDescriptions.graph_action: A graph build, traverse, update or prune.
x-enumDescriptions.scorer_step: One stage of a scorer's pipeline.
x-enumDescriptions.guardrail: A safety or policy check, and whether it tripped.
x-enumDescriptions.retrieval: A generic retrieval that is not vector-store specific.
x-enumDescriptions.mapping: An inline data transform between pipeline stages.
x-enumDescriptions.skill_resolution: A dynamic resolver deciding which skills an agent may use.
x-enumDescriptions.workspace_action: A filesystem, sandbox, search or computer-use action.
x-enumDescriptions.http_request: An outbound HTTP call made on the agent's behalf.
x-enumDescriptions.generic: Anything else. Always valid; never inferred.

x-enumDescriptions.unset: Still running, or the producer never said.
x-enumDescriptions.cancelled: Abandoned deliberately, by a caller or a timeout.

SignalType.description: The six signals mcpd stores. Every one of them is correlated by trace id, most of them by span id as well, and every one of them passes through the same redaction pipeline.

x-enumDescriptions.span: A unit of work with a start and, usually, an end.
x-enumDescriptions.score: A machine evaluation of a span or trace.
x-enumDescriptions.feedback: A human evaluation of a span or trace.
x-enumDescriptions.aspect_note: One sentence recorded against a trace along one aspect. Stored, redacted and retained like the other five, and erased with the subject it belongs to.

x-enumDescriptions.trace: Finer than debug. Off by default.

x-enumDescriptions.gauge: A point-in-time value. Aggregates by last, min, max or mean.
x-enumDescriptions.histogram: A distribution. Aggregates by bucket, and answers quantiles.

SamplingKind.description: How mcpd decides which traces to keep.

x-enumDescriptions.always: Keep everything. The default, and correct until volume says otherwise.
x-enumDescriptions.never: Keep nothing. Useful to disable a single project without redeploying.
x-enumDescriptions.ratio: Keep a fixed fraction, decided once at the root so a trace is never half-recorded.
x-enumDescriptions.deterministic: Keep a fixed fraction, decided by hashing the trace id. Every collector in a fleet makes the same decision without coordinating.
x-enumDescriptions.tail: Buffer the trace, then decide once it finishes. Keeps every error and every slow trace regardless of rate.

RedactionMode.description: What happens to a value a redaction rule matched.

x-enumDescriptions.drop: Remove the key entirely, as if it was never sent.
x-enumDescriptions.mask: Replace the whole value with a fixed token.
x-enumDescriptions.partial: Keep a documented prefix and suffix, mask the middle. Enough to recognise a value without disclosing it.
x-enumDescriptions.hash: Replace with a keyed SHA-256 digest. Equal inputs stay equal, so you can still group and join, but the original cannot be recovered.

ScoreSource.description: Where a score came from. Kept separate from the scorer's identity so the same scorer can run in more than one context.

x-enumDescriptions.live: Produced online, as the traced run happened.
x-enumDescriptions.offline: Produced later, by scoring stored traces.
x-enumDescriptions.experiment: Produced by an experiment run against a dataset.
x-enumDescriptions.manual: Entered by a person, through the API or the UI.

ScorerKind.description: How a scorer reaches its answer.

x-enumDescriptions.code: Deterministic code in the daemon. Free, and gives the same answer twice.
x-enumDescriptions.judge: A built-in rubric graded by the configured judge model, in steps: preprocess, analyze, score, reason.
x-enumDescriptions.criterion: A criterion the operator wrote under `judge.criteria`, graded by the judge model in one call.

ScoreDirection.description: Which way a scorer's value is better. A comparison reads a fall in `toxicity` as an improvement and a fall in `faithfulness` as a regression.

x-enumDescriptions.higher_is_better: A larger value is a better run.
x-enumDescriptions.lower_is_better: A smaller value is a better run, as for `toxicity`, `bias` and `hallucination`.

FeedbackKind.description: The shape of a human judgement.

x-enumDescriptions.rating: Ordinal. `value` is a number inside the scale the producer declares.
x-enumDescriptions.tag: A label chosen from a set. `value` is the label.
x-enumDescriptions.comment: Free prose, with no score attached.

EntityKind.description: The named thing a span belongs to. Bounded and low-cardinality, so it is safe as a metric label.

x-enumDescriptions.service: A plain service with no richer identity.

ExperimentStatus.description: Where an experiment run has got to.

AuditResult.description: Whether authorisation let the request through.

x-enumDescriptions.allowed: The key carried the scope the endpoint needs, so mcpd went on to handle the request.
x-enumDescriptions.refused: Authorisation refused the request before it reached storage. Recording the attempt is the point of the row.

RunStatus.description: Where a run is. Only `running` can move; the other four are terminal, and a terminal run holds no deadline, no wait and no live attempt.

x-enumDescriptions.running: Making progress, or waiting for something that will move it: a lease, a timer or an event.
x-enumDescriptions.succeeded: Reached the end of the graph. `output` holds what the definition's `output` template rendered, when it declares one.
x-enumDescriptions.failed: Ended on an error nothing handled: a step that failed under `on_error: fail_run`, a spent ceiling, or a cancelled child. `error` says which.
x-enumDescriptions.timed_out: Ended because the run's own deadline passed.
x-enumDescriptions.cancelled: Ended because a caller asked, through the cancel endpoint or by cancelling an ancestor run.

AttemptStatus.description: Where one attempt at one step is. Four states are live and four are terminal, and the daemon never shows a live attempt on an ended run.

x-enumDescriptions.pending: On disk and offerable to a worker, once its retry timer, if any, has fired.
x-enumDescriptions.leased: Held by a worker that has not yet posted `started`.
x-enumDescriptions.started: Held by a worker that has posted `started`, so a body is running.
x-enumDescriptions.orphaned: The lease expired with no heartbeat. Not offerable while the reclaim window is open: a heartbeat inside the window restores the attempt, and a window that closes with no contact requeues it or fails the run, depending on `effect` and on whether the body had started.
x-enumDescriptions.failed: Finished with an error, or marked failed because the run ended while the attempt was live.
x-enumDescriptions.timed_out: The step's own deadline passed before the attempt ended.
x-enumDescriptions.skipped: Never ran, because the step's `when` guard was false.

StepKind.description: What a step attempt is an attempt at. `task` and `agent` are claimable. A `wait` row is written by the event that resumes it or the deadline that ends it, so a wait's output and status read like any other step's.

x-enumDescriptions.task: Claimable work. The worker runs whatever code it registered under this step id.
x-enumDescriptions.agent: Claimable work whose body is the worker's own agent loop. Identical on the wire to `task`; the kind is recorded so the trace and the interface can tell an agent turn from a plain step.
x-enumDescriptions.wait: A suspension the daemon resumes on an event or ends on a deadline. Never offered to a worker.

ConstructKind.description: What a run's cursor names: the construct at its current position in the definition's `steps`. Every kind except `end` is a node kind a definition can declare.

x-enumDescriptions.agent: Claimable work whose body is the worker's agent loop.
x-enumDescriptions.sleep: A relative delay, in milliseconds. No process is alive during it.
x-enumDescriptions.sleep_until: An absolute delay, to an RFC 3339 instant rendered from a template.
x-enumDescriptions.wait_event: A suspension addressed by an event name and a key rendered per run.
x-enumDescriptions.parallel: A fixed fan-out over named branches, each branch one claimable step. Done when every branch has ended.
x-enumDescriptions.foreach: A fan-out over the items of an array, each item one claimable step, with at most `concurrency` of them offerable at once.
x-enumDescriptions.loop: A bounded loop whose body is one claimable step per iteration, ended by `until` or by `max_iterations`.
x-enumDescriptions.subworkflow: A child run of another definition. Its output becomes this step's output, and a cancel walks down into it.
x-enumDescriptions.end: The end of the graph. Never declared in a definition: the cursor reaches it when the last step has ended.

Effect.description: What running a step body twice would cost, which is what the daemon branches on when a lease is lost. Default `at_least_once`.

x-enumDescriptions.at_least_once: Running the body twice is acceptable. A lost lease requeues the attempt. The default.
x-enumDescriptions.at_most_once: Running the body twice is not acceptable. `started` must be posted before the body runs, and a started attempt whose lease is lost fails the run rather than running again.

TimerKind.description: Every deadline the daemon keeps. Each one is a row the tick fires, and each firing is a transaction that moves the run.

x-enumDescriptions.lease_expiry: A lease that has not been heartbeated. Firing moves the attempt to `orphaned` and opens a reclaim window one lease length long.
x-enumDescriptions.reclaim: The close of the reclaim window an expired lease opened. Firing requeues the attempt or fails the run, depending on `effect` and on whether the body had started.
x-enumDescriptions.step_timeout: One attempt's ceiling, from the node's `step_timeout_ms`. It bounds a worker that heartbeats for ever.
x-enumDescriptions.wait_timeout: A `wait_event` whose event has not arrived by `timeout_ms`.
x-enumDescriptions.retry: The backoff before a requeued attempt becomes claimable. Firing writes the next attempt as `pending`.

RunEventKind.description: What a row in a run's event log records. Every row is written in the transaction that made the change it describes, so a reader that has seen sequence number n has seen every change below it.

x-enumDescriptions.run_cursor: The cursor moved. Payload: `index`, `construct`, and `step_key` when the construct has one.
x-enumDescriptions.step_leased: A worker claimed an attempt. Payload: `step_key`, `attempt`, `worker_id`.
x-enumDescriptions.run_resumed: An event resumed a waiting run. Payload: `step_key`, `event_id`.
x-enumDescriptions.run_ended: The run reached a terminal status. Payload: `status`, and `error` when there is one.

DefinitionKind.description: What kind of thing a definition describes.

x-enumDescriptions.workflow: A graph of steps the daemon walks. The only kind in version 1: `agent` definitions arrive with the in-process agent loop, which is not served yet.

EventOutcome.description: What the daemon did with a published event.

x-enumDescriptions.delivered: A waiting run took it and moved, in the same transaction.
x-enumDescriptions.parked: No run was waiting. The event is held for 24 hours for the next run that reaches a matching wait with `accept_parked`.
x-enumDescriptions.duplicate: This event id has been seen before, so nothing was written. The publish endpoint says when a derived id is treated this way.

ConflictReason.description: Why a worker call about a lease answered 409. Each reason tells the worker something different to do next.

x-enumDescriptions.fenced: A later attempt exists, or another lease terminated this attempt. Abandon the work and post nothing more for this lease.
x-enumDescriptions.already_applied: This lease's own earlier `complete` or `fail` landed and its reply was lost. The step is done; `attempt_status` says how. Post nothing more.
x-enumDescriptions.not_started: `complete` or `fail` arrived for a `leased` attempt under `at_most_once`. A bug in the worker: post `started` first, and log it loudly.
x-enumDescriptions.run_terminal: The run has ended. Stop, and stop claiming for this run.

StepErrorClass.description: How a step failed, which decides whether the daemon retries it.

x-enumDescriptions.retryable: Worth another attempt. The daemon retries while attempts remain, at the node's backoff, and honours `retry_after_ms` when it is larger.
x-enumDescriptions.fatal: Another attempt would fail the same way. No retry; the node's `on_error` applies.
x-enumDescriptions.invalid_input: The step's input cannot be acted on. No retry; the node's `on_error` applies.
x-enumDescriptions.unservable: This worker does not serve the definition version, or does not recognise the step key. The attempt returns to `pending` after one lease length without spending the retry budget, so another worker can take it.
x-enumDescriptions.cancelled: The worker gave the attempt up on request. No retry; the node's `on_error` applies.

OnError.description: What happens to a run when a node fails after its retries. Default `fail_run`.

x-enumDescriptions.fail_run: End the run `failed`, with the step's error message as the run's error.
x-enumDescriptions.continue: Mark the step `failed` and move on, so a later `when` guard can read `steps.<id>.status` and `steps.<id>.error`.

Backoff.description: How the delay between retries grows.

x-enumDescriptions.exponential: Each retry waits twice as long as the last, starting at `initial_ms` and capped at `max_ms`.

WaitTimeout.description: What a `wait_event` node does when its deadline passes with no event. Default `fail`.

x-enumDescriptions.fail: The node fails. Its `on_error` decides what the run does next.
x-enumDescriptions.continue: The wait ends and the run moves on to the next node.

ValueKind.description: The JSON type of a value. Used where mcpd reports the shape of something it holds without returning the thing itself.

x-enumDescriptions.number: The value was a JSON number.
x-enumDescriptions.string: The value was a JSON string.
x-enumDescriptions.array: The value was a JSON array.
x-enumDescriptions.object: The value was a JSON object.

MonitorWatch.description: What a monitor measures over its window.

x-enumDescriptions.error_rate: The fraction of runs that failed, 0 to 1.
x-enumDescriptions.latency_p95: Run duration at the ninety-fifth percentile, in milliseconds.
x-enumDescriptions.trace_count: How many runs happened. Catches a pipeline that has gone silent.
x-enumDescriptions.score_mean: The mean of the scorer named by `scorer_id`.
x-enumDescriptions.step_count_divergence: How far a run strays from the usual shape of its own definition. This watch sets no threshold in steps, because a step count is never high in absolute terms, only high for that definition. It reads the recent completed runs of one definition version, takes the median step count as the usual shape, and reports a run whose modified z-score against the median absolute deviation exceeds the monitor's bound, 3.5 by default. The median absolute deviation is used rather than a mean and a standard deviation because it tolerates up to half its sample being outliers, which is the case here: a runaway cohort must not be allowed to redefine normal. Fewer than twelve completed runs and the watch says nothing rather than guessing. A run that takes several times its usual number of steps trips this long before it reaches `max_steps`, and while its error rate is still zero.
x-enumDescriptions.run_repetition: How much a run repeats itself. For each run in the window, the highest number of attempts it made at any one node of its definition, counting a retry and a loop iteration of that node alike; the watch reads the mean of that number. One means no node ran twice. A loop that re-enters the same node, and a retry storm, both raise this before either reaches `error_rate`.

MonitorCompare.description: Which way a monitor's threshold is breached.

x-enumDescriptions.above: Trip when the value rises above the threshold.
x-enumDescriptions.below: Trip when the value falls below it. This is the direction that catches a quality regression, and a silent pipeline.

MonitorCondition.description: Where a monitor or an objective stands. A tripped condition latches: it stays tripped until the number recovers, and too little data never clears it, because silence is not recovery.

x-enumDescriptions.acknowledged: Tripped, acknowledged, and still breaching. Returns to `nominal` on its own when the number recovers.
x-enumDescriptions.insufficient: Not enough data in the window to judge. Also the state before the first evaluation.

TextSearch.description: What the `q` parameter matches on this deployment's storage backend. Reported by `GET /v1/api/capabilities` so a search box can say what it searches instead of leaving a reader to infer it from a result set.

x-enumDescriptions.none: `q` is not applied at all. No backend that ships declares this; a backend that did would be telling an interface to hide its search box rather than let somebody type into one that returns everything.
x-enumDescriptions.substring: `q` matches anywhere inside a word, so `heck` finds `checkout`.
x-enumDescriptions.words: `q` matches whole words only, which is what a person typing two words into a search box expects. There is no stemming: `refund` does not find `refunds`.

Partitioning.description: How the storage backend cuts each signal table on its anchor time. It decides whether expiring a day of data is a metadata operation on one part or a row-by-row delete.

x-enumDescriptions.none: One table, no partitions. Retention removes rows.

Facet.description: A dimension a filter box can offer values for. The set is closed on purpose: each one is a column or a parsed field the daemon keeps a distinct-value list for as signals arrive, so answering is a read of a small table rather than a scan of every span in the retention window.

x-enumDescriptions.entity_kind: The kind of thing a step was: an agent run, a tool call, a retrieval, and so on.
x-enumDescriptions.entity_name: The name of that thing, such as the tool that was called.
x-enumDescriptions.service_name: The service that reported the signal.
x-enumDescriptions.environment: The environment it came from, such as `production`.
x-enumDescriptions.tag: A tag carried on a run.
x-enumDescriptions.metric_name: A metric name, for the name box of a chart.
x-enumDescriptions.metric_label_key: A label key a metric point carries. Project-wide: these are every key seen in the project, not the keys of one named metric.
x-enumDescriptions.metric_label_value: A value one label key takes. Needs `key`, because the answer would otherwise be every value of every label mixed together.

DeltaSignal.description: A signal that can be polled for what has arrived. Only the three that carry a server-set arrival time: a score and a piece of feedback are stamped with the caller's own timestamp, so a watermark over them would either skip a late row or repeat every row for ever.

x-enumDescriptions.traces: The run projection, which is what a run list refreshes from.
x-enumDescriptions.spans: Steps, for a waterfall that is still filling in.

AspectReadiness.description: How far the daemon has got with one aspect for one entity. It is computed from the rows that are stored and never recorded, so it cannot go stale, and it is per entity and per aspect rather than global: one agent can have goal themes to read while its behaviour notes are still collecting.

x-enumDescriptions.collecting: Fewer notes than a clustering pass needs. The floor is 50 notes for one aspect on one entity, and below it the daemon writes no snapshot at all rather than sorting a handful of sentences into themes nobody should draw a conclusion from.
x-enumDescriptions.processing: Enough notes to cluster, and no snapshot covers this aspect yet. The next pass will write one. Nothing is wrong and nothing needs doing.
x-enumDescriptions.ready: A snapshot covers this aspect, so themes exist and every theme route answers.

ThemeState.description: What happened to a theme between the previous snapshot and this one. The daemon matches themes across consecutive snapshots by their wording, so a theme keeps its id while its wording holds, and this records what that match found. It is computed from the two clusterings alone and never from a trace attribute.

x-enumDescriptions.birth: The first snapshot this theme appears in.
x-enumDescriptions.continue: Present in the previous snapshot and in this one, matched to the same id. The ordinary state of a theme that is holding together.
x-enumDescriptions.split: The previous snapshot held one theme where this one holds several. The history point's `split_from` names the theme it came out of.
x-enumDescriptions.merge: Several themes in the previous snapshot are one theme here. The history point's `merged_from` names them.
x-enumDescriptions.resurrection: Present in an earlier snapshot, absent from the one immediately before this, and back now under its original id. A theme that comes and goes reads as one theme with gaps rather than as several short-lived ones.
x-enumDescriptions.death: The theme was in the previous snapshot and is in none of this one's clusters. Reachable only through a theme's history: a dead theme has no row in the snapshot it died in, so it is never a node in a flow.

ThemeNodeKind.description: What one node of a theme flow stands for. A stage holds its themes, at most one noise node and at most one overflow node, and the three together account for every trace in the stage, which is what lets the shares add up to one.

x-enumDescriptions.theme: One theme. It carries a `theme_id`, so it can be filtered on, opened and followed through its history.
x-enumDescriptions.noise: The notes in this stage that joined no theme. Noise is not a failure bucket: it holds rare requests, wording nothing else matched and patterns that have not recurred yet, and a large noise share means varied traffic or too few notes rather than something going wrong. Its notes are read from the examples route with `noise` as the theme id.
x-enumDescriptions.other: The themes past `theme_limit_per_stage`, folded into one node so the stage totals still add up. It carries no `theme_id` and cannot be selected, filtered on or opened, because it is a presentation fold and not a group of anything.

SnapshotLandmarkReason.description: Why one snapshot is in a landmark selection. A timeline draws a couple of dozen points over a range that may hold thousands of passes, so the daemon chooses them and says why, rather than handing back the newest few and leaving the reader to assume that is the whole story.

x-enumDescriptions.range_start: The oldest snapshot in the requested range. Always included, so a timeline starts where the range does.
x-enumDescriptions.range_end: The newest snapshot in the requested range. Always included, so a timeline ends at the current state.
x-enumDescriptions.time_sample: Chosen to spread the remaining points evenly over the range. Sampling is by time and not by ordinal, so an hour of frequent passes does not crowd out a quiet week.

KeyScope.description: What an account API key may do. The same six scopes the daemon's configured keys carry, under the same names as the `auth` value of each endpoint.

x-enumDescriptions.ingest: Write signals, and read nothing. The key that lives in every process that emits a span.
x-enumDescriptions.read: Read stored signals: runs, spans, logs, metrics, scores, analytics and datasets.
x-enumDescriptions.write: Change stored data: scores, feedback, datasets, experiments and acknowledgements.
x-enumDescriptions.admin: Delete data and read the audit log. Also accepted where `execute` or `worker` is needed.
x-enumDescriptions.execute: Start, cancel and signal runs, and publish events to them.
x-enumDescriptions.worker: Claim steps and report their outcome. The key that lives in the process running step bodies.

InputTokenDetails.description: Input tokens broken down by how the provider billed them. Every field is optional; absent means the provider did not report it, which is different from zero.

text.description: Ordinary text tokens: not cached, not audio, not image.

cache_read.description: Tokens served from a prompt cache. Usually billed at a large discount.

cache_write.description: Tokens written into a prompt cache. Usually billed at a premium.

cache_write_5m.description: Tokens written to a five-minute ephemeral cache, where the provider prices TTLs separately.

cache_write_1h.description: Tokens written to a one-hour ephemeral cache.

image.description: Image input tokens, including rendered PDF pages.

OutputTokenDetails.description: Output tokens broken down by kind.

reasoning.description: Hidden reasoning tokens. Billed, and usually invisible in the response.

TokenUsage.description: Token counts for one model call. Totals are authoritative; the detail breakdowns explain them and are what cost is actually computed from.

total_tokens.description: Input plus output, when the provider reports a total that differs from the sum.

input_details.description: How the input tokens were billed.

output_details.description: How the output tokens were billed.

Cost.description: What a span cost, in a single currency. mcpd computes this from a price book at ingest and stores the result, so a later price change never silently rewrites history.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code. `USD` unless the price book says otherwise.

total_cost.description: The sum, including any meter that is neither input nor output.

price_book.description: Identifier of the price book used, so a figure can be traced back to the rates that produced it.

is_estimated.description: True when mcpd derived the cost from a price book, false when the producer reported it directly.

ModelParameters.description: The sampling settings a caller chose for one model call. Recorded because a run nobody can reproduce is a run nobody can debug, and the seed and the sampling settings are what a replay has to match. Every field is what the caller asked for, never what the provider did with it. None of them carries prompt or completion text, so a producer running with payload capture off still records all of them.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature the caller asked for. Absent when the caller left the provider's default in place, which is not the same as sending zero.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling: the caller asked the sampler to consider the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities reach this fraction. Absent when the caller set none.

top_k.description: The caller asked the sampler to consider only this many of the most likely tokens. Not every provider offers it.

max_tokens.description: The ceiling the caller put on output length. An answer that stops in the middle of a sentence usually stopped here, and this is the first field to read when one does.

seed.description: The sampling seed the caller passed. Nothing in mcpd reads it. It is recorded because without it a run cannot be reproduced at all, and a comparison between two runs that differ only in their seed is worth nothing.

stop_sequences.description: The stop sequences the caller supplied. They are short strings the caller wrote, so they are settings rather than payload, and an answer that ends early often ends on one of them. Do not put prompt text here.

has_response_format.description: True when the caller constrained the output to a fixed shape, such as a JSON schema or a grammar. The shape itself is not recorded: it can be large and it is caller-owned content, and what a reader needs is whether the constraint was on.

message.description: A human-readable message. Required: an error with no message is not actionable.

kind.description: The error class or code, such as `RateLimitError` or `ECONNRESET`.

stack.description: A stack trace, when the producer captured one.

retryable.description: Whether the producer considered the failure worth retrying.

details.description: Structured detail. Passes through redaction like any other payload.

Correlation.description: The descriptive context a signal belongs to. Every field here is queryable and most are safe as metric labels; the high-cardinality ones (`user_id`, `session_id`, `request_id`) are queryable but blocked from metric labels by the cardinality filter.

project.description: Which project this belongs to. The primary tenancy key.

service_version.description: The emitting service's version, so a regression can be pinned to a release.

session_id.description: A user-facing session. Groups many traces into one conversation.

thread_id.description: A conversation thread within a session.

user_id.description: The end user. Hashed with a keyed digest at ingest, so runs can still be grouped by customer without storing who the customer is. Filtering on it hashes your query value the same way, so lookup keeps working. Rotating the key deliberately breaks the link.

resource_id.description: A tenant or workspace inside the calling application.

run_id.description: The producer's own identifier for this run.

request_id.description: The inbound request that caused this work.

experiment_id.description: Set when the run was produced by an experiment.

release.description: A release or git sha, for regression attribution.

SpanLink.description: A reference from this span to another, in this trace or a different one. Links express causality that parentage cannot: a batch job caused by twenty requests has twenty links and one parent.

span_id.description: The linked span, when the link points at one rather than a whole trace.

kind.description: Why the link exists, such as `follows_from`, `retry_of` or `replay_of`.

Page.description: Cursor pagination. Cursors are opaque and stable; never construct one by hand.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Absent on the last page.

total.description: Total matching rows, when the backend could count them cheaply.

IngestBatch.description: One batch of signals sent to the native ingest endpoint. Any combination of the six signals may appear in a single batch; mcpd sorts them out. Supplying `ingest_key` makes the whole batch idempotent, so a client that retries after a timeout never double-counts.

aspect_notes.description: Aspect notes to record. A note is a sentence about a trace, so it arrives with that trace's other signals, under the same idempotency key and through the same redactor.

ingest_key.description: Idempotency key for this batch. Replaying a batch with a key mcpd has already accepted is a no-op that still returns 200.

IngestError.description: Why one signal in a batch was refused.

signal.description: Which signal kind the failure was in.

index.description: Position within that signal's array, so a client can find the offending record.

message.description: What was wrong, in terms the sender can act on.

IngestResult.description: What mcpd did with a batch. Counts are per signal, and `rejected` is never silently zero: a signal mcpd could not store is always reported with a reason.

duplicate.description: How many were recognised as a replay of an already-accepted batch and skipped.

errors.description: One entry per rejected signal, naming what was wrong and where.

traces.description: The matching traces, in the requested order.

TraceDetail.description: One trace and everything attached to it.

spans.description: Every span, ordered by start time then by depth, so a waterfall renders without sorting.

MetricSeriesPoint.description: One bucket of an aggregated series.

count.description: How many raw observations fell in this bucket. Distinguishes a genuine zero from no data.

exemplar_trace_id.description: A trace that contributed to this bucket, so a spike on the chart opens the run that caused it.

MetricSeries.description: One line on a chart: a single label combination over time.

labels.description: The label values that identify this series.

bucket.description: The bucket width actually used, which may differ from the request when mcpd chose it.

LatencyStats.description: Latency distribution over a window, in milliseconds.

mean.description: Arithmetic mean. Reported alongside quantiles, never instead of them.

GroupedStat.description: One row of a grouped breakdown.

key.description: The group's value, such as a model id.

count.description: How many runs fell in this group.

AnalyticsSummary.description: Headline numbers for a window. One request backs the overview screen.

error_rate.description: Failures as a fraction of runs, between 0 and 1.

CostBucket.description: Spend in one time bucket for one group.

key.description: The group this row belongs to.

currency.description: Currency of every figure in this response.

series.description: A time series, when `bucket` was supplied.

deleted.description: How many records were removed, across every signal.

HealthStatus.description: Whether the server is alive and able to serve.

version.description: The mcpd version serving this request.

spec_version.description: The data-model spec version this build implements. A client can refuse to talk to an incompatible server.

uptime_seconds.description: How long this process has been running.

detail.description: What is degraded, when something is.

signup.description: True when this daemon offers open sign-up: anyone may create an account at `POST /v1/api/account/signup` and log in at `POST /v1/api/account/login`. Absent when it does not, which is the default. The interface reads this to decide whether to show its sign-up and log-in screens.

ScorerInfo.description: One scorer mcpd can run, as described to a caller.

id.description: Stable identifier, recorded on every score it produces.

description.description: What it measures, in one line.

needs_config.description: Whether it needs settings to mean anything. A scorer that needs an expected answer cannot run without one.

kind.description: How the scorer reaches its answer.

direction.description: Which way its value is better.

config_keys.description: The `ScorerConfig` settings it reads. Empty when it needs none.

available.description: Whether this daemon can run it now. A judged scorer is unavailable until a `judge` block names an endpoint and a model.

ScorerConfig.description: Settings shared by the scorers that need them. Every field is optional; a scorer that needs one and does not get it declines instead of guessing.

needle.description: Text the answer must contain, for `contains`.

max_cost.description: A budget in currency units, for `cost_budget`.

max_tool_calls.description: The most tool calls a healthy run should make, for `tool_efficiency`.

span_kind.description: The kind of span that must be present in the run, for `span_present`.

span_name.description: The span name that must be present in the run, for `span_present`. Matched exactly against `Span.name`.

tool_name.description: The tool that must have run and ended `ok`, for `tool_succeeded`. Matched exactly against the `name` of a span whose kind is `tool_call`, `client_tool_call`, `provider_tool_call` or `mcp_tool_call`.

forbidden.description: Text the answer must not contain, for `excludes`. Any one of them fails the run.

keywords.description: Words or phrases the answer should mention, for `keyword_coverage`. The score is the share that appear.

pattern.description: A regular expression the answer must match somewhere, for `matches_pattern`.

expected_tools.description: The tools the run should call, for `tool_call_accuracy`, and the order it should call them in, for `tool_order`. Matched exactly against tool-call span names.

forbidden_tools.description: Tools the run must not call, for `tool_not_called`.

min_chars.description: The shortest acceptable answer in characters, for `answer_length`.

max_chars.description: The longest acceptable answer in characters, for `answer_length`.

json_schema.description: A JSON Schema the answer must satisfy, for `json_schema`. `type`, `properties`, `required`, `items`, `enum`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `minLength`, `maxLength` and `additionalProperties: false` are checked.

context.description: The passages the answer should rest on, for the judged scorers that read context. When empty, the outputs of the run's `retrieval` and `rag_vector_operation` spans are used.

ScoreRunRequest.description:
A request to run scorers over runs that are already stored.

Scoring reads stored runs rather than running inline, so an evaluation can never add latency to the request it is judging, and a scorer that fails can never fail a user's request.

project.description: Which project's runs to score. Defaults to the server's default project.

trace_ids.description: Score exactly these runs. Takes precedence over the window.

from.description: Otherwise, score runs started after this time.

limit.description: Most runs to score in one request, newest first, when `trace_ids` is empty. Unset, it is 100 for deterministic scorers, and for a pass with a judged scorer it is as many runs as fit in the request deadline. A judged pass that names more runs than fit, through `limit` or `trace_ids`, is refused with the cap.

scorers.description: Which scorers to run, by id. Empty means every scorer that needs no configuration.

config.description: Settings for the scorers that need them.

source.description: What to record as the origin of these scores.

dry_run.description: Report what would happen and store nothing.

SkippedScorer.description: A scorer that declined to answer on one run.

reason.description: Why. Never silent: a scorer that cannot answer is more interesting than one that returned a number.

skipped.description: Every scorer that declined, with its reason.

scores.description: The scores themselves, so the caller sees them without a second read.

ScorerDelta.description: How one scorer moved between two experiments.

baseline_mean.description: Mean on the baseline, when it ran there.

decidable.description: Whether the sample is large enough for the delta to mean anything. A deliberately blunt rule rather than a significance test: below twenty observations on either side, mcpd says the comparison is not decidable rather than dressing noise up as a finding.

direction.description: Which way this scorer's value is better, from the catalogue. Scorers the daemon does not know read as higher is better.

ci_low.description: Lower end of the 95% confidence interval on `delta`, from Welch's t-test. Absent when either side has fewer than two observations.

p_value.description: Two-sided p-value for the difference in means.

regressed.description: Whether this scorer moved the wrong way: decidable, and the whole interval on the worse side of zero.

ExperimentComparison.description:
Two experiments, compared.

The point of an experiment is the comparison, so this reports the delta per scorer beside the sample sizes. A mean that moved on four runs is noise, and printing the counts next to it is what stops it being read as a result.

scorers.description: One row per scorer present on either side.

regressed.description: Whether any decidable scorer moved down.

CaptureRequest.description: A request to turn stored runs into dataset cases.

trace_ids.description: The runs to capture. Each becomes one item, keeping its trace id so anyone can go back and read what actually happened.

use_output_as_expected.description: Record each run's own output as the expected answer. Leave this off for a run that went wrong: capturing a bad answer as the reference would enshrine the bug.

CaptureResult.description: What a capture added to a dataset.

requested.description: Runs asked for. A gap means a run was not found.

ItemsAdded.description: How many cases a dataset gained.

ErasureResult.description: What an erasure request removed, counted per signal. The subject is not echoed back: it has been erased, and repeating it in a response that may be logged on the way out would write it down again.

project.description: The project the erasure ran in. No other project was read or touched.

spans.description: How many spans were removed, with the prompts and completions they carried.

logs.description: How many log lines were removed.

metrics.description: How many metric points were removed.

feedback.description: How many pieces of feedback were removed.

deleted.description: The total across every signal, so a caller that wants one number does not add them up.

runs_erased.description: How many durable runs were removed from the run store, each with its step attempts, event log, deadlines, waits, the events it consumed and any span still queued for the trace store. A run is matched on the `user_id` in its correlation, as it was started with it, and removed with the whole tree of subworkflow runs it belongs to. Not part of `deleted`, which counts the trace store. Absent when this daemon does not serve runs.

runs_in_flight.description: How many runs attributed to this person were left untouched because a run in their tree has not ended. Removing a live run would corrupt the workflow it is part of, so these are counted rather than skipped in silence, and `note` names the root runs. Cancel them, or let them end, then send the erasure again. Absent when this daemon does not serve runs.

aspect_notes_erased.description: How many aspect notes were removed, matched by the run they describe and by the person stamped on them. Not part of `deleted`. Absent only from a store that holds no notes.

dataset_items_erased.description: How many dataset cases captured from an erased run were emptied in place. They are not deleted, because a case was kept on purpose, so they are not part of `deleted`.

datasets.description: The datasets those emptied cases sit in, so the reply can say where they are.

deletes_pending.description: True when the storage backend applies the deletes after this reply is sent, as ClickHouse does, so the counts say what matched rather than what has already left the disk.

unmatchable_identifiers.description: How many stored identifiers this request could not have matched, because they were written in the other form, hashed or plain, from the one given. A number above zero means the counts may not be the whole answer.

note.description: Why the numbers above may not be the whole answer, in sentences an operator can repeat. Absent when they are the whole answer.

DefinitionDocument.description: A definition as you post it: the graph, and the id and version to store it under. The body is validated at write time against `spec/definition.schema.json`; a body the walker cannot run is refused with a 400 naming the field, and unknown fields are refused, so a guard that is spelled wrong is an error and not a run that skips its guard.

id.description: The definition's identifier within its project. Matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.

kind.description: What kind of definition. Absent means `workflow`, the only kind version 1 serves.

version.description: The version to store the body under. Absent asks the daemon to choose: the version whose stored body is identical, or one past the highest stored. A named version that is free is taken; one held by an identical body is confirmed; one held by a different body is a 409, because a stored version never changes.

body.description: The document itself: `input_schema`, `limits`, `steps` and `output`. The definition schema names every field.

version.description: The version the body is stored under.

assigned.description: True when the daemon chose the number because the body was new. False when the body already existed at this version, or you named the version yourself.

RunCursor.description: The frontier of a run: which position in the definition's `steps` it has reached, and what sits there.

index.description: The index into `steps`, or their count at the end of the graph.

step_key.description: The step this position belongs to, when the construct has one. A fan-out names its parent step; the branch and item keys are on the attempts.

RunTimer.description: A deadline the daemon holds for a run.

step_key.description: The step the deadline belongs to. Absent for a run-level deadline.

RunWait.description: A suspension waiting for an event.

event.description: The event name an inbound event must match.

key.description: The rendered key that picks this run out of every run waiting on that event.

expires_at.description: When waiting stops and the node's `on_timeout` applies.

RunDetail.description: One run and everything the daemon holds for it.

attempts.description: Every attempt, in the order they were written.

timers.description: The deadlines currently held. Empty once the run has ended.

waits.description: The suspensions currently open. Empty once the run has ended.

RunEventPage.description: A page of a run's event log.

events.description: The rows after the requested sequence number, in order.

has_more.description: Whether rows beyond the last one here existed when the page was read. A run that is still moving will write more.

CauseLink.description: One edge of a cause chain: an ancestor step, and the template path through which the step below it read that ancestor's output. An ancestor read through two paths appears twice, once per path.

step_key.description: The ancestor step, keyed the way the journal keys it: `refund/issue`, `classify[3]`, `poll[7]/classify`.

status.description: Where the ancestor's latest attempt ended.

attempts.description: How many attempts were made at the ancestor. More than one on a step that ended `succeeded` is worth reading: it got there, but not the first time.

template_path.description: The path as the definition writes it inside `${...}`, such as `steps.classify.output.kind`. The definition declares this edge, so the chain is read rather than inferred from timing.

consumed_by.description: The step key that read this ancestor through `template_path`. On a direct edge it is the step the answer is about; deeper in the chain it is another ancestor.

depth.description: How far this ancestor sits from the step the answer is about. `1` is read directly, `2` is read by something the step read directly, and so on.

silent_producer.description: True when this ancestor ended `succeeded` and every step between it and the failed step ended `succeeded` too. Nothing on that path is marked failed, so no status code points at it and the value it produced is the suspect. It is not the same as `status` being `succeeded`: an ancestor sitting behind a step that did fail is not a silent producer, because that failure already explains the run.

value_kind.description: The JSON type `template_path` resolved to on the ancestor's stored output. The value itself is never returned, only its shape. Absent when there is no output to read, which is the case for a step that never ran and for one that failed.

value_empty.description: True when that value was null, an empty string, an empty array or an empty object. A step that ended `succeeded` and handed the step below it nothing is the failure a status code cannot catch, and this is the field that shows it. Absent for the same reason `value_kind` is.

StepCause.description: Why one step of a run failed, answered by walking backwards along the data dependencies its definition declares. The daemon reads the run journal and the pinned definition version, both of which it has to hold to render `${...}` templates at all, so this answer is available with span payload capture off and with no model, prompt or completion involved.

run_id.description: The run this answer is about.

step_key.description: The step this answer is about, as it was asked for.

status.description: Where that step's latest attempt ended.

attempts.description: How many attempts were made at it.

error.description: Why the latest attempt failed, when it did. Absent on a step that did not fail, because the endpoint answers for any step, not only a failed one.

chain.description: The ancestors whose output this step consumed, directly or transitively. Ordered by `depth` ascending, then by the order the paths appear in the definition, so two calls against one run return the same list in the same order. Empty when the step reads nothing but the run input.

truncated.description: True when the walk stopped at `max_depth` with ancestors left unvisited, so `chain` is a prefix of the answer rather than the whole of it.

StartRunRequest.description: A request to start a run.

project.description: Which project. A selector: refused with 403 on a mismatch with the key's grant, filled in for a single-project key, and a 400 when a multi-project key names none.

version.description: Which version. Absent pins the highest stored version at this moment, and the run records it.

input.description: The run's input. Validated against the definition's `input_schema` when it declares one; a failure is a 400.

correlation.description: Context to store on the run and copy onto every span the daemon writes for it. `project` and `run_id` inside it are ignored: the run's own values win.

idempotency_key.description: Makes the start idempotent per project for 24 hours: a repost returns the same run and starts nothing, and two simultaneous posts of one key produce one run.

project.description: Which project. A selector: refused with 403 on a mismatch with the key's grant, filled in for a single-project key, and a 400 when a multi-project key names none.

worker_id.description: Who is asking. Recorded on the attempt as `lease_owner` and in the run's event log. Nothing else about the worker is stored.

max.description: The most leases to hand back, 1 to 100.

wait_ms.description: How long to hold the request open waiting for work, 0 to 60000 milliseconds. The daemon holds a claim for at most four fifths of its request timeout, 24000 at the default 30 seconds, so a longer wait is answered early rather than cut off with a 503. An empty answer means nothing became runnable in time: reissue the claim.

run_id.description: Restrict the claim to one run, which is how a script drives its own run inline.

StepLease.description: A step handed to a worker. Every later call about the attempt is addressed by `lease_id`.

lease_id.description: The address of every later call about this attempt.

project.description: Which project the run belongs to.

definition_id.description: Which definition the run is executing.

definition_version.description: Which version. Fail the lease with class `unservable` if you do not serve it.

step_key.description: The step to run. A worker that does not recognise it fails the lease with class `unservable` rather than guessing.

kind.description: Whether this is a plain task or an agent turn.

attempt.description: Which attempt this is. The fence: a call about this lease is refused once a later attempt exists.

effect.description: Under `at_most_once`, post `started` and wait for its 200 before running the body.

expires_at.description: When the lease lapses. Heartbeat every `heartbeat_ms` to keep it.

deadline_ms.description: The step's own timeout, when the node declares one. It bounds the attempt whatever the heartbeats say.

idempotency_key.description: A key stable across every attempt of this step: the SHA-256 of `run_id:step_key`. Pass it to any downstream call that can deduplicate.

input.description: The node's `input` template rendered for this attempt, or the run's input when the node declares none.

prior.description: The ended attempts of earlier steps, keyed by step id: `{ status, output?, error? }` for the latest attempt of each, or `{ status: skipped }`. Only ended attempts appear.

state.description: The run's state object as it stands.

correlation.description: The run's correlation, with `run_id` set. Put it on every span you record inside this step.

trace_id.description: The run's trace. Set it on every span you record inside this step.

span_id.description: The span the daemon has already opened for this attempt. Set it as `parent_span_id` on your own spans, so a model call or a tool call nests under the step.

parent_span_id.description: The run's root span, which this attempt's span hangs off.

leases.description: Zero to `max` leases. Empty when nothing became runnable within `wait_ms`.

reclaimed.description: True when this call found the attempt `orphaned` and restored it to the state it came from.

StepUsage.description: Token usage a worker reports on `complete`. The daemon prices it from its price book and charges the attempt, the run and the root of the run tree.

total_tokens.description: Input plus output, when the provider reports a total that differs from the sum.

input_details.description: How the input tokens were billed.

output_details.description: How the output tokens were billed.

model.description: The model that produced the usage, which the price book needs to price it.

provider.description: The provider that served the model.

StepResult.description: What a worker posts to complete a step.

output.description: The step's output. Later steps read it as `steps.<id>.output`.

state.description: An object to merge shallowly into the run's state.

usage.description: Token usage to price and charge.

StepError.description: Why a step failed, as the worker reports it.

class.description: What kind of failure. Decides whether the daemon retries.

message.description: What went wrong, for the person reading the run.

details.description: Structured detail. Stored on the attempt.

retry_after_ms.description: The least the daemon should wait before the next attempt, when the worker knows: a rate limit's reset, say. Honoured when it is larger than the backoff. At most 315360000000 (3650 days), the bound on every duration in a definition; a larger value is a 400 naming this field.

StepFailure.description: What a worker posts to fail a step.

run_status.description: Where the run is after this call.

next.description: `claim` when more work is runnable now, `idle` otherwise.

attempts_left.description: After a `fail`: how many attempts the node's retry budget still allows.

StepConflict.description: The body of a 409 from a worker call. `reason` says what is true and what the worker should do next.

attempt_status.description: Where that attempt is, when it still exists. Under `already_applied` this says how the step ended.

PublishEventRequest.description: An event for whichever run is waiting for it.

project.description: Which project. A selector: refused with 403 on a mismatch with the key's grant, filled in for a single-project key, and a 400 when a multi-project key names none.

event.description: The event name, matched against open waits.

key.description: Matched against the rendered `key` of each waiting run. Delivered to the matching run whose wait expires soonest.

event_id.description: Your own id for this event. A supplied id seen before answers `duplicate` and writes nothing, whether or not a run is waiting. Absent, the daemon derives one from `project`, `event`, `key` and `payload`, and a derived id counts as a duplicate only when no run is waiting, because two identical approvals for two runs on one key are two events. Send your own id from any handler that can be retried.
The id used, supplied or derived.

SignalRequest.description: An event for one run, addressed by run id rather than by key. The daemon reads the run's open wait on `event`, takes its key, and routes the event as a published one.

event.description: The event name. The run must hold an open wait on it.

event_id.description: Your own id for this event, deduplicated as on a published event.

WorkerRegistration.description: A worker announcing the definitions it serves.

project.description: Which project. A selector: refused with 403 on a mismatch with the key's grant, filled in for a single-project key, and a 400 when a multi-project key names none.

worker_id.description: Who is registering. Not stored: dispatch reads the runnable set, never a worker table.

definitions.description: Each is stored under the versioning rule, exactly as if posted to the definitions endpoint.

registered.description: Where each definition landed, in the order posted.

lease_ttl_ms.description: How long a lease lasts without a heartbeat.

heartbeat_ms.description: How often to heartbeat a held lease: a third of `lease_ttl_ms`.

Monitor.description: A saved condition the daemon evaluates on a schedule. Monitors are configured in the daemon's configuration file, not through the API.

name.description: What a person should read when it trips.

window_seconds.description: How far back each evaluation looks.

min_samples.description: The fewest runs the window must contain before the monitor will trip. Without it a single failed run in a quiet hour is a 100% error rate, and the first thing anyone does with an alert that cries wolf is mute it.

webhook.description: Where to POST when it trips or clears. Set as a full URL in the config file; the API returns only its host, because a webhook URL is often its own credential.

enabled.description: Whether it is evaluated at all.

value.description: The measured value, when there was enough data to measure one.

samples.description: How many runs the window held.

MonitorState.description: A monitor and the condition it is latched in.

last.description: The most recent reading. Absent before the first evaluation.

tripped_at.description: When it first tripped, while it stays tripped.

Slo.description: A service level objective: the fraction of runs that must succeed over a window. A monitor asks whether a number is over a line right now. An objective asks whether the promise is going to be missed and how fast the error budget is burning, over two windows at once, so a two minute blip and a slow leak get the different answers they need. Objectives are configured in the daemon's configuration file, not through the API.

objective.description: The fraction of runs that must succeed, between 0 and 1. `0.995` is ninety-nine and a half percent of runs.

window_days.description: How long the promise is measured over.

min_samples.description: The fewest runs a burn window must hold before it may trip.

webhook.description: Where to POST on a transition. Set as a full URL in the config file; the API returns only its host, because a webhook URL is often its own credential.

enabled.description: Whether it is evaluated at all.

success_rate.description: The observed success rate over the whole window.

budget_remaining.description: The fraction of the error budget still unspent. Negative once it is overspent, which says by how much the promise was missed.

burn_fast.description: The burn rate over the one hour window. A rate of 1 spends the whole budget exactly over the whole window.

burn_slow.description: The burn rate over the six hour window. Both windows must exceed their trip rate together before the objective trips, which is what stops a brief spike paging anyone.

SloState.description: An objective and the condition it is latched in.

last.description: The most recent reading. Absent before the first evaluation.

tripped_at.description: When it first tripped, while it stays tripped.

StoreCapabilities.description: What the storage backend behind this daemon can and cannot do. Three backends implement one storage trait and they are not equal: a reader on ClickHouse who searches for `CAFE` with an acute and finds nothing has no way to learn that this backend folds ASCII case and no more. Read this once at connect time and offer only what the deployment answers. Every field is named after the capability an endpoint names when it refuses with 501, so the two can be compared without translation.

backend.description: Which backend this describes: `sqlite`, `postgres` or `clickhouse`. The same string `/healthz` reports as `storage`.

unicode_case_folding.description: Whether `q` folds case for letters outside ASCII. False means a search for `CAFE` with an acute does not find the lowercase form, which a reader otherwise meets as an empty result they cannot explain.

immediate_deletes.description: Whether a delete is on disk when the call returns. False means the backend accepted the delete and applies it afterwards, so a count says what matched rather than what has already gone.

discovery.description: Whether `GET /v1/api/discovery` answers. False means a filter box has to be filled from what is already on screen.

discovery_label_values.description: Whether the `metric_label_value` facet is answerable, not only the keys. Separate because the values are the expensive half: a key set is small and bounded, and a value set is not.

delta_polling.description: Whether `GET /v1/api/deltas` answers, so a list refreshes from a cursor rather than by running the whole query again.

per_signal_retention.description: Whether retention can carry a different window per signal. False means one window covers all five.

declarative_retention.description: Whether the window can be handed to the database engine, so nothing has to run a delete on a timer.

partitioning.description: How the signal tables are cut on their anchor time.

partition_drop_retention.description: Whether a retention pass can drop a whole partition instead of deleting rows one at a time.

idempotent_schema_init.description: Whether a start with nothing to apply issues no schema statement at all. False means every process replays the schema on every boot, which is harmless on one node and is metadata churn across a replicated deployment.

theme_analysis.description: Whether this deployment answers the Intelligence endpoints. False means the store holds no note or theme tables and every one of those routes refuses with 501 naming this capability, so a client decides once whether to offer the feature rather than showing a reader an empty page they cannot account for. Every backend that answers gives the same themes: the clustering runs in the daemon over stored notes and not in SQL, so there is nothing here for a backend to do differently.

DiscoveredValue.description: One value a filter dimension takes in a project.

value.description: The value, exactly as it is stored, so it can be sent straight back as a filter with no further mapping.

last_seen.description: When mcpd last received a signal carrying it. This is arrival time and not the signal's own timestamp, so a backfill of last year's data does not make a value look current. Carried so a caller can rank down or grey out a value nothing has reported for a month. Values are ordered by `value` and not by this: a list somebody reads alphabetically is stable between polls, and one ordered by recency reshuffles under them as data arrives.

DiscoveryResponse.description: The values one filter dimension takes, for a filter box. Answered from a distinct-value list the daemon maintains as signals arrive, not by scanning the signal tables, because the question is asked on every keystroke and the tables it would otherwise scan are the largest thing the deployment holds.

key.description: The label key the values belong to, echoed back for `metric_label_value`. Absent for every other facet.

values.description: The values, ordered by value, ascending.

DeltaResponse.description: What has arrived since a cursor. A poll is not a page: paging walks a fixed result set backwards in the sort you chose, and polling walks forwards in arrival order and never ends, so the two cursors are different things and are deliberately not interchangeable. Rows come back oldest arrival first, so applying them in order to a list you already hold gives the same result as having listed afresh.

signal.description: Which signal these rows are. Exactly one of the three arrays below is present, and it is this one.

cursor.description: Where the next poll resumes. Always present, and unchanged from the request when nothing came back: moving it forward on an empty poll is what would drop a row that lands a moment later with an earlier arrival time. Treat it as meaningless, and send back the one you were given.

has_more.description: True when the page filled and more is waiting, so a caller draining a backlog polls again at once rather than waiting for its next tick.

traces.description: The runs that arrived, when `signal` is `traces`.

spans.description: The steps that arrived, when `signal` is `spans`.

logs.description: The log lines that arrived, when `signal` is `logs`.

AspectLimits.description: The bounds a clustering pass runs under. They are published because each one changes what a reader is looking at: a floor that has not been reached means no themes at all rather than an empty result, and a ceiling that has been reached means every share is a share of what was read. They are copied from the divergence watch, which is the one windowed statistic mcpd already ships. `pass_armed` is the first of them to read: the other three describe what a pass would do, and it says whether one runs.

min_notes_to_cluster.description: How many notes one aspect on one entity needs before a pass runs at all, 50 by default. Below it the aspect reads `collecting` and no snapshot is written.

max_notes_per_pass.description: The most notes one pass reads, 20,000 by default, taken newest first. A window holding more is clustered from the newest of them and its snapshot is marked `capped`.

page_size.description: How many notes the pass reads at a time while it fills a window, 500 by default. It bounds what the pass holds, not what it covers.

max_aspects.description: How many aspects one project may define, the four built-ins included. It is configuration and is published here so a client that lets an operator add an aspect knows when to stop instead of finding out from a refusal.

pass_armed.description: Whether this deployment runs the clustering pass at all. False means no snapshot will ever be written however many notes arrive, so every aspect stays `collecting` or `processing` for ever and no theme route will have anything to answer with. It is configuration and not a fault, and it is not the same thing as the 501 the theme routes give: that says the storage backend cannot hold the tables, which nobody can switch on, while this says nobody has switched the pass on yet. It is published here rather than on every progress row because it is one fact about the deployment, and a client reads this route once to learn what the aspects are called.

AspectCatalogue.description: Every aspect a project describes traces along, with the bounds the clustering pass runs under. The four built-ins are rows in the same table as anything you define, so there is no fallback list inside a client that can quietly disagree with this one.

aspects.description: The aspects, in `sort_order`. Disabled aspects are included, because notes already recorded under one stay readable and a name that vanished from this list would make them look like a mistake.

limits.description: The bounds a pass runs under in this deployment.

EntityIndexRow.description: One entity that has aspect notes, with the roll-up a list needs to be worth reading. A row appears as soon as the first note is recorded, before any theme exists, because an empty screen with a count moving on it is a different thing from an empty screen and a reader has to be able to tell them apart.

entity_kind.description: The kind of thing this row is about.

trace_count.description: How many of its traces carry at least one note. This is not the entity's trace count: writing a note lags ingestion, so a busy agent can show far fewer here.

note_count.description: How many notes are recorded about it.

enabled_aspects.description: How many aspects are switched on for this entity's project.

ready_aspects.description: How many of those have themes to read. The two numbers read as `2 of 4` and are the honest answer to whether this row is worth opening yet.

readiness.description: The row's overall state, which is the least advanced of its enabled aspects, so a row says `processing` while any one of them is still short of a snapshot. It never reports the best case.

last_note_at.description: When the newest note about this entity was recorded, so a reader can tell a list that is filling from one that stopped.

latest_snapshot_at.description: The cutoff of this entity's newest snapshot. Absent until a pass has written one, which is the ordinary state of a row that is still collecting.

EntityIndexResponse.description: A page of the entities that have aspect notes.

entities.description: The matching entities, most recently written to first.

AspectProgressRow.description: How far one aspect has got for one entity. Counted from stored notes, so it is what has happened and not a projection of what will.

aspect.description: Which aspect this row is about.

readiness.description: The state this aspect is in for this entity.

note_count.description: How many notes are recorded along it.

trace_count.description: How many distinct traces those notes were written about.

notes_needed.description: How many more notes this aspect needs before a pass will run. Zero once the floor is reached, which is what turns a wait into a number a reader can watch.

last_note_at.description: When the newest note along this aspect was recorded. Absent when there are none.

AspectProgress.description: What the daemon has recorded for one entity, aspect by aspect. This is the answer to why a themes screen is empty, and it separates the three cases that look identical on screen: nothing has been recorded, enough has been recorded and no pass has run yet, or there are themes to read and the reader is looking at the wrong aspect.

entity_kind.description: The kind of entity this describes.

readiness.description: The entity's overall state, which is the least advanced of its enabled aspects.

trace_count.description: How many of this entity's traces carry at least one note.

aspects.description: One row per enabled aspect, in catalogue order.

latest_snapshot.description: The newest snapshot for this entity, when a pass has written one. Absent while every aspect is still collecting.

SnapshotLandmark.description: One snapshot in a timeline, with the reason it was chosen.

reason.description: Why this snapshot is in the selection. Present for `presentation=landmarks` only; an inventory returns consecutive snapshots and chooses nothing, so there is nothing to report.

SnapshotListResponse.description: A selection of one entity's snapshots, oldest first, so a timeline can be drawn without reordering anything.

total.description: How many snapshots the entity has in the requested range. This is the number the selection was drawn from and not the number returned, so a timeline can say what it is standing in for.

ThemeNode.description: One node of one stage of a flow: a theme, the stage's noise, or the overflow the stage folded away.

node_id.description: Identifies this node inside this flow, and is what a link names at either end. It is not a theme id: the noise and overflow nodes have one of these and no theme id.

kind.description: Whether this node is a theme, the noise or the overflow.

theme_id.description: The theme this node stands for. Present only when `kind` is `theme`, which is what makes the other two impossible to drill into by accident.

label.description: What to show for this node: a theme's own label, or the words for noise or overflow.

trace_count.description: How many traces this node accounts for.

coverage.description: This node's share of the stage's traces, between 0 and 1. A stage's nodes cover all of it, so its shares add to 1.

ThemeStage.description: One aspect's column in a flow. Stages come back in the order the aspects were asked for, and links only ever join neighbouring stages, so the order decides which co-occurrences are visible and is not a display preference.

trace_count.description: How many traces this stage accounts for.

nodes.description: The stage's nodes, largest first, with the noise and overflow nodes last.

ThemeLink.description: A ribbon between one node of a stage and one node of the next. It says the two describe the same traces and nothing more: a link between a goal theme and an outcome theme means they were written about the same runs, not that one caused the other.

source_node_id.description: The node this link leaves, in the earlier stage.

target_node_id.description: The node it reaches, in the next stage.

trace_count.description: How many traces are assigned to both ends.

source_share.description: That count as a fraction of the source node's traces, between 0 and 1.

target_share.description: That count as a fraction of the target node's traces, between 0 and 1. The two shares differ whenever the nodes are different sizes, and reading only one of them is how a thin ribbon gets mistaken for a weak relationship.

ThemeFlow.description: One snapshot read across two to four aspects at once: a stage per aspect, and the links between neighbouring stages. Association, never causation.

snapshot.description: The snapshot this flow was computed from, so every count on the page can be read against the window it came from.

stages.description: One stage per aspect, in the order they were asked for.

links.description: The links between neighbouring stages. There are none between stages that are not neighbours, which is why the order of the aspects matters.

ThemeDetail.description: One theme in one snapshot, or the answer that this snapshot did not hold it.

snapshot.description: The snapshot that was read, with its own counts, so a caller can write `28 of 70 traces in this window` without a second request.

theme.description: The theme, when this snapshot holds it. Absent is an answer and not an error: the theme did not exist in that window, which is what scrubbing a timeline back past a theme's birth looks like. A theme id this entity has never had is a 404 instead.

ThemeExample.description: One note from a theme, with the run it was written about. The two ids are different things: `note_id` identifies the sentence and `trace_id` identifies the run it describes.

trace_id.description: The trace the note was written about.

text.description: The sentence, after redaction. This is the wording that put the trace in this theme, so a reader can see why it landed here rather than take it on trust.

similarity.description: How much this note's wording overlaps the theme's label, counted out of 64. It is a count of shared sketch positions and not a percentage, and it is an integer on purpose: no part of the clustering uses floating-point arithmetic, so two replicas cannot order the same notes differently.

trace_started_at.description: When the run began, so examples can be read against the period they came from rather than against when the note was written.

ThemeExampleListResponse.description: A page of the notes behind one theme.

examples.description: The notes, most like the theme's label first.

ThemeHistoryPoint.description: One theme in one snapshot of its life. Every count belongs to that snapshot alone, and windows overlap, so a run of these is read as a series and never added up.

snapshot_id.description: The snapshot this point comes from.

cutoff_at.description: When that snapshot became the current state.

window_from.description: Start of that snapshot's window, inclusive.

window_to.description: End of that snapshot's window, exclusive.

state.description: What had happened to the theme by this point.

note_count.description: How many notes were in the theme here.

trace_count.description: How many distinct traces those notes were written about.

coverage.description: The theme's share of the notes that snapshot read for this aspect, between 0 and 1. Coverage and raw count can move in opposite directions, and coverage is the one that says whether a theme is gaining ground.

split_from.description: The themes this one came out of at this point. Empty unless `state` is `split`.

split_into.description: The themes that came out of this one at this point. Both directions are stored, so a caller never has to read a second theme's history to learn what happened to this one.

merged_from.description: The themes that became this one at this point. Empty unless `state` is `merge`.

merged_into.description: The theme this one became at this point, when it stopped being its own theme.

ThemeHistory.description: One theme across every stored snapshot that holds it, oldest first. This is the only theme response that names no single snapshot, because the series is the answer.

theme_id.description: The theme this history is of.

aspect.description: The aspect it was clustered along.

label.description: The theme's label at its newest point. A label can change between snapshots, because the note most like the others can change while the theme holds together.

points.description: The series, oldest first, so nothing has to be reordered before it is drawn or differenced.

TraceAspectNotes.description: Every aspect note recorded about one trace, which is at most one per aspect. Read it beside the trace itself: a note is the sentence that put this run in each of its themes, so it is the shortest route from a theme back to what actually happened.

trace_id.description: The trace these notes are about.

notes.description: The notes, in catalogue order. Empty when nothing has written one yet, which is ordinary for a recent trace.

AccountCredentials.description: An email address and a password, for sign-up and for log-in.
